goal: A pull request the runner will not land does not park its project in silence. Today it does: `landPr` (`src/mc/run.js`) logs `#N left open — <reason>` and moves on, `inFlight` (`src/mc/run-plan.js`) then refuses every later round because the PR is open, and the only trace is a runner.log line and a runs.tsv note — `success,open,gate-red`, `plan-trespass`, `open,not-a-stack`. Counted on 2026-09-03..04: of 55 step rows, 5 ended `plan-trespass` and 2 `open,gate-red`; each of those seven projects stood still until a person read the log, found the reason, fixed the branch by hand and ran `mc merge` (#11274, #11275, #11276, #11300, #11301, #559, #561 — every one of them, in one evening).

Martin, 2026-09-04: *"vi behöver ett enkelt kunna fånga upp vilka processer som står i check_before_merge; kanske en ny status + en särskilt prompt instruktion till brief att detta kan behöva göras av brief. Annars är nog det bästa att check av merge görs av respektive plan; om det nu skulle vara kod-relaterat."*

So: the runner remembers why it left a PR open, the page and the brief show it, and the project itself gets one repair session — the way a merge conflict already gets a reconcile session — before a person is asked. What a repair cannot fix goes to the brief as one proposal, not a log line.
contract: **The runner still writes no plan.** `held before merge` is mc's own state under `~/mc/runner/`, like `current-<repo>.json` — never a status in `PLAN.json`. `STEP_STATUSES` stays `ready`/`done`/`blocked`; Martin's *"kanske en ny status"* is answered by a file the page reads, not a fourth status the runner would have to write into a plan.

**The gate decides; the repair obeys it.** A repair session makes the branch green or admits it cannot; it never merges, never lowers a threshold, never deletes a test to pass. A repair that would need a decision blocks the step with `blocked_by` the way any step does.
**One repair per pull request.** A PR that is still held after its repair session is a person's, through the brief. No loop.
**One step, one PR.** `mc` prints the page and `mc run --rounds 1` completes a round after each. No force-push, no rewritten history; everything lands through `mc merge`.
out_of_scope: **Making the gate greener.** The SQL snapshot treadmill (`docs/plans/sql/` goes stale whenever memoro's main moves) and `sql:admission` are memoro's own; a repair session runs the repository's own scripts for them and nothing here changes the scripts.

**`mc merge` at a terminal waiting for a held gate.** The runner's `landPr` waits (since #571); the verb a person types still refuses and says who holds it. That is a separate, smaller change if it is wanted.
**A held PR's *contents* being judged by mc.** Whether a red test is the change's fault is the repair session's reading, never a rule here.

success_criteria.criterion: Every pull request the runner left unlanded is listed, with its reason, without anyone reading runner.log.
success_criteria.check: `mc --json` carries `queue.held` — `{ project, pr, reason, note, since, repairs }` per PR — and the page's QUEUE section draws `held before merge N` with each project, PR and reason under it. Driven by a fixture in `tests/mc/page.test.js`, and seen on the page after a real `open,gate-red`.

success_criteria.criterion: A project whose PR is held gets one repair session, told exactly why the PR was held, and the runner lands the PR when the repair made it green.
success_criteria.check: `tests/mc/run.test.js`: a round on a project with a held PR runs a `repair` session whose prompt carries the PR number, the branch and the reason; a second round on the same PR runs no second repair. runs.tsv rows with `kind` `repair`.

success_criteria.criterion: The brief sees what a repair could not fix, and its role tells it what to do with it.
success_criteria.check: `~/mc/brief/<date>.md` has a *Held before merge* section listing each such PR with reason, repairs tried, and the branch; `canon/roles/brief.md` says these are the brief's to decide — merge by hand, close, or block the step — one proposal each.

success_criteria.criterion: `docs/technical/mc-run.md` says what `held` is, when a repair runs, and where it stops.
success_criteria.check: The section exists on main and names the file, the kind and the one-repair rule.

documents.label: How the runner lands and what it leaves

steps.title: The runner remembers why it left a pull request open, and the page says so
steps.done_when: `~/mc/runner/held.json` lists every PR `landPr` did not land with its reason, is cleared when that PR lands or closes, `mc --json` carries it as `queue.held`, and the page's QUEUE section draws `held before merge N` with project, PR and reason — all driven by tests.
instruction: **Where the fact is born.** `landPr` in `src/mc/run.js` ends with `const note = landingNote(report)` and three branches: `merged`, `off-<branch>`, and `else say(\`${name}: #${pr} left open — ${report?.reason …}\`)`. That `else` is the only place the runner knows a PR is held and why. Write it there: `~/mc/runner/held.json`, one entry per PR — `{ project, pr, branch, reason, note, since, repairs: 0 }` — through `writeJson` like the other runner files. The trespass path is the other birthplace: in `runStep`, `note = 'plan-trespass'` with the `problems` lines; write those as the reason. `no-json`/timeout with a PR open counts too: reason `session timed out with the PR open`.

**Where it dies.** An entry leaves the file when its PR is no longer open — the round already asks GitHub what is open (`queue()`, `PR_LIST_ARGS`) — or when `landPr` lands it. Reconcile the file against the open list once per round in `queue()` so a PR merged or closed by hand disappears the next round. Keep it in `chores()` order-independent: any lane may write it, so read-modify-write through one function with `writeJsonAtomic` (`src/mc/atomic-write.js`).

**The page.** `queueSection` in `src/mc/page-collect.js` already carries `skipped` and `stale` under QUEUE; add `held` beside them and draw it in `queueLines` (`src/mc/page-render.js`) as `held before merge N` on the heading's count line, with one row per PR under the skips: `<project>  #<pr>  <reason clipped>`. Yellow, like `blocker finished`: it waits on somebody. `mc --json` gets it for free through the section. Fixtures: `tests/mc/page.test.js` builds `queueSection` inputs directly — add `held` to `DATA` and to the painted snapshot; `tests/mc/run.test.js` has the `rounds` fixture that makes a merge round report `stopped_at: 'red'` — assert the file after such a round.

**What not to do.** No new step status, no write into any `PLAN.json`. The file is mc's, beside `runner.json` and `current-*.json`, and `docs/technical/mc-ui.md` § *Where the facts come from* gets a row for it.
comments: The rules are `src/mc/held.js`, pure over the entries; `run.js` reads-changes-writes the file through `hold()`, `release()` and `reconcileHold()` and nothing else, and `createRunner()` returns `held()` for a reader. Every entry carries `repo` as well as the fields the instruction named: two repositories number their pull requests independently, so `samePr` is repo *and* number — memoro #9 and memoro-cli #9 are different work, and a release keyed on the number alone would have dropped the wrong one.

The reconcile is in `queue()` rather than in `chores()`. That is where the round already asks GitHub what is open (`PR_LIST_ARGS`), and a lane's round calls `queue({ only })`, so a lane reconciles only the repository it asked about; a repository `gh` could not be answered for is *unknown* rather than empty, and nothing of its is dropped on a bad network. `chores()` calls `queue()` too, so the whole file is still swept once a round.

For step 2: `holdPr` keeps `since` and `repairs` when the same pull request is held again, so bumping `repairs` before the repair session starts (as the instruction wants) survives the next round's re-hold. `holdReason({ note, problems })` and `holdsAfterSession(note)` in held.js are the words a repair prompt should carry — for `plan-trespass` the `unauthorisedChanges` problems are already inside `reason`, and `note` is the runs.tsv-shaped word (`open,gate-red`, `plan-trespass`, `timeout`, `open,not-a-stack`, `open,stack-stopped`). Step 3 should read the file through `heldPath(root)` + `heldEntries`/`parseHeld` rather than parsing it again.

Criterion 1 is left `met: false` on purpose: the fixture half is done (`tests/mc/page.test.js`, section and painted snapshot), but no real `open,gate-red` existed to see on the page — the runner has landed everything it started since. What was seen instead is the whole path end to end: a `held.json` written by hand under a throwaway `MC_WORK_ROOT`, and `mc` drawing `QUEUE  empty … · held before merge 1` with the project, `#11274` and the reason under it. The close-out step should tick it when a real one has been seen, or say it was the fixture.

steps.title: A held pull request gets one repair session
steps.done_when: A round on a project whose PR is in `held.json` with `repairs: 0` runs a `repair` session in that workarea — told the PR, the branch and the reason — bumps `repairs`, and lands the PR if the session made it green; a project with `repairs >= 1` is skipped with a line saying it waits for the brief. Driven by tests, with a `canon/roles/repair.md`.
instruction: **The shape already exists: reconcile.** `chooseKind` (`src/mc/run-plan.js`) returns `{ kind: 'reconcile' }` when the merge of origin/main stopped on conflicts, `runStep` builds `reconcilePrompt` for it, and `canon/roles/reconcile.md` is its role. Repair is the same shape for a different stop: `inFlight` (`src/mc/run-plan.js`) refuses a project with an open PR; before that refusal, ask `held.json` — if the PR is there with `repairs: 0`, the kind is `repair`, not a skip. `repairs >= 1` stays a skip, with the line `#N is held before merge after a repair — the brief's` so the log says why nothing happens.

**The prompt.** `repairPrompt({ name, repo, pr, branch, reason, note })` in `run-plan.js`, beside `reconcilePrompt`: *You are in the `<name>` workarea of <repo>, on branch `<branch>`, whose pull request #<pr> the runner would not land: <reason>. Make it green and push to the same branch — the runner lands it after you. Do not open another pull request, do not merge, do not touch a threshold or delete a test to pass. If the reason is `plan-trespass`, the problems are named: undo the change to any step that is not yours and keep your own step's `status`, `pr` and `comments`. If green needs a decision — an SQL admission, a contract — set your step `blocked` with `blocked_by` and say what the answer is about.* The role file `canon/roles/repair.md` carries the method the other roles carry (a turn is the cost; `Read`/`Grep`; run the selection once).

**The session must see what the gate saw.** `reason` from the merge round is the headline (`2 tests red: …, … and 4 more`); the full red list is in `~/.memoro/mc/gate-rounds.jsonl` for that PR (`red_names`) and the gate's own output in the round's `--json`. Put the red names in the prompt — all of them, not the headline's five — and for a command gate its captured output (`extra_gates[].output`, `repo-gate.js:806`). A repair told `sql:pr-ci — exit 1` and nothing else will guess; on 2026-09-03 that gate's stderr was lost and three rounds were retried on a stale GitHub head before anyone knew why.

**After the session.** `runStep` already asks GitHub what is open and calls `landProject` when the note is `success`; a repair session's success is the same path. Bump `repairs` before the session starts, not after — a session killed on its budget must still count. Land through the same `landPr`, which waits for a held gate.

**Tests.** `tests/mc/run.test.js`: (1) a project whose PR is held with `repairs: 0` gets a `repair` session whose prompt carries `#N`, the branch and the reason, and its runs.tsv row says `repair`; (2) with `repairs: 1` no session runs and the log line names the brief; (3) the trespass reason reaches the prompt with its problems; (4) a repair that lands clears the entry. `tests/mc/run-plan.test.js` for `repairPrompt`.

steps.title: The brief takes what a repair could not fix
steps.done_when: `~/mc/brief/<date>.md` has a *Held before merge* section — project, PR, branch, reason, repairs — for every entry in `held.json` with `repairs >= 1`, and `canon/roles/brief.md` says these are the brief's to decide, one proposal each: merge by hand, close, or block the step with a decision.
instruction: **The digest.** `src/mc/brief-collect.js` gathers the brief's first message from `runs.tsv`, the plans and the proposals (`parseRuns`, `listPlans`, `listProposals`); the writer that assembles the sections is in the same file or `commands/brief.js` — find it, and add *Held before merge* after the runner's day. Read `held.json` through the same helper step 1 wrote; do not parse runs.tsv notes to reconstruct it.

**The role.** `canon/roles/brief.md` gets one paragraph: a PR held before merge after its repair is the brief's, and the answer is one of three — `mc merge <repo> <pr>` by hand when the red is not the change's (say why), `gh pr close` with a line in the step's `comments` when the work is wrong, or the step set `blocked` with a `blocked_by` decision when it needs Martin. One proposal per PR, never a menu; a held PR that is not in the brief is a project standing still that nobody has been told about.
**The page.** Nothing new: step 1's `held before merge` line is what a person sees between briefs. If the count is above zero at the top of a brief, the brief opens with it.

**Tests.** Whatever `brief-collect` already has for its sections (`tests/mc/brief-collect.test.js`): a `held.json` with one entry at `repairs: 1` and one at `repairs: 0` yields a section naming the first only.

steps.title: Close-out
steps.done_when: `docs/technical/mc-run.md` has a section *Held before merge* — the file, when a repair runs, the one-repair rule, and where the brief takes over — the criteria are `met` where they are, and the plan is `done`.
instruction: Write the section in `docs/technical/mc-run.md` beside *The merge*, and the `held.json` row in `docs/technical/mc-ui.md` § *Where the facts come from* if step 1 did not. Set `met` on the criteria this project actually met, with the check done as written — the page seen with a real held PR if one exists, the fixture otherwise, and say which. The runner archives the plan and writes the `project_log.md` row when every step is `done`.
